# Keybindings

<!-- Generated by the test `keybinding_page_tests` in `crates/bongos/src/zed`. Do not edit by hand: run that test with BONGOS_UPDATE_KEYBINDINGS_PAGE=1 to rewrite this file. -->

bongos has three keybinding profiles: Emacs, Vim and VS Code (the `base_keymap` setting, or the keybindings picker). Every bongos command is bound under all three. The commands are bound once, in the Emacs keymaps under `ctrl-c`; the Vim and VS Code keys are derived from those rows when the keymap loads, so a command added to the Emacs keymap gets its Vim and VS Code keys with no further work.

Each cell reads `Linux / macOS`. Every command is also in the command palette and in `M-x` under every profile.

| `artifact::HideAll` (`w shift-h`) | `ctrl-c w shift-h` / `ctrl-c w shift-h` | `ctrl-k b w shift-h`, `space w shift-h` / `cmd-k b w shift-h`, `space w shift-h` | `ctrl-k b w shift-h` / `cmd-k b w shift-h` |

## Profile rules

- **The leaders.** Emacs binds the commands under `C-c`. VS Code binds them under `ctrl-k b` (`cmd-k b` on macOS), in the same contexts. Vim binds both of those and also `space` in normal and visual mode (and in the prompt editor's normal mode for the prompts commands).
- **The `space` delay.** Vim's own `space` moves the cursor right. Because `space w w` and the other chords start with `space`, a lone `space` waits for the chord timeout before it moves; type the chord or wait.
- **Prompt editor.** The chat prompt editor is a full editor. Under Vim it opens in normal mode: `i` enters insert, `Escape` returns to normal, and `ctrl-k b ctrl-c` (`space ctrl-c` in normal mode) sends. Under VS Code the default editing keys apply, so `ctrl-c` copies, and `ctrl-k b ctrl-c` sends.
- **Terminals.** Under VS Code and Vim a terminal forwards keys to the shell: the bongos leaders are not bound there, and `ctrl-c`, `ctrl-d`, `ctrl-w`, `ctrl-r` and `escape` reach the shell. The one way out is `alt-1` (`cmd-1` on macOS), which focuses the first editor pane. Chat terminals follow the same rule. Commands from a terminal go through the command palette (`ctrl-shift-p`, `cmd-shift-p`).
- **Panel keys.** The single keys of the bongos panels live in the specific overrides files (`assets/keymaps/specific-overrides.json` and `specific-overrides-macos.json`), which every profile loads after its base keymap, so they work under every profile. A panel key added later goes in those files, not in the Emacs keymap. They are:

| Panel context | Key | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ChatList` | `/` | `chat::Filter` |
| `ChatList` | `a` | `chat::Archive` |
| `ChatList` | `f` | `chat::ForkToTask` |
| `ChatList` | `r` | `chat::Rename` |
| `ChatList` | `t` | `chat::ToggleAllTasks` |
| `ChatList` | `u` | `chat::Restore` |
| `LandingView` | `r` | `project::ResolveSplit` |
| `ProposalView` | `^` | `proposal::Up` |
| `ProposalView` | `enter` | `proposal::Descend` |
| `RunView` | `a` | `workflow::Approve` |
| `RunView` | `enter` | `workflow::OpenLogs` |
| `RunView` | `g` | `workflow::ToggleGraph` |
| `RunView` | `l` | `workflow::OpenLogs` |
| `RunView` | `v` | `workflow::Revise` |
| `RunsPanel` | `a` | `workflow::Approve` |
| `RunsPanel` | `enter` | `workflow::OpenLogs` |
| `RunsPanel` | `l` | `workflow::OpenLogs` |
| `RunsPanel` | `v` | `workflow::Revise` |
| `WorkPanel` | `^` | `work::Up` |
| `WorkPanel` | `tab` | `work::ToggleRow` |

- **Your `keymap.json`.** It loads last, so a binding of yours wins over every profile at the same context depth.
- **Linux exceptions.** Under VS Code the Linux and macOS keymaps bind the same commands, with `ctrl` read as `cmd`; these are the differences, because Linux terminals and window managers reserve some chords:

| Where | Linux | macOS | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal: leave for the first editor pane | `alt-1` runs `workspace::ActivatePane` | `cmd-1` runs `workspace::ActivatePane` | the Linux `Pane` context binds `alt-1` to its own item, so the terminal row restores the way out; macOS already has `cmd-1` |
| Terminal: `ctrl-k` / `cmd-k` | `ctrl-k` runs `terminal::SendKeystroke` | `cmd-k` runs `terminal::Clear` | Linux terminals forward `ctrl-k` (readline's kill-line) to the shell instead of holding the `ctrl-k b` leader; on macOS `cmd-k` clears the terminal, as it does in VS Code, and `ctrl-k` is no chord prefix |
